newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL DEBT OUTLOOK-Issuers timid after stock drop.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL DEBT OUTLOOK-Issuers timid after stock drop.

text.p: Brazilian debt issuers, who were punished last week for pricing $700 million in new paper amid a five-day rollercoaster ride in local stock markets, were seen sitting the week out.
"Hopefully, we won't see any new issues come this week. The market doesn't need any new paper," said a Eurobond trader in Sao Paulo.

Despite last week's 15 percent stock market dive, issuers went ahead with a number of new deals, most of which promptly traded down, market players said. Brazilian Eurobond spreads widened about 15 basis points on average on devaluation fears triggered by recent currency turmoil in Asia.
Trikem, a PVC pipe maker, placed a $250 million 10-year bond with a five-year call, at a spread of 437 basis points priced to maturity. The issue was trading at 450 bps on Monday.
The Republic of Brazil priced a 150 million 10-year sterling bond at 275 bps over U.K. gilts. The issue soon widened by about 15 bps.
Construction firm Camargo Correa's $150 million eight-year bond, with puts and calls at five years, came at a spread of 245 bps priced to the put.
"The timing was the worst. Last week was just chaos and it came at a time when the market was already doing poorly because of oversupply in new issues," said one Brazilian debt watcher.

Private power firm Escelsa from the state of Espirito Santo, however, did delay its $350 million 10-year Eurobond because of stock volatility. The deal, managed by Morgan Stanley, was expected to come later this month or in August.
Players said it could take a month before the market could absorb the supply of new paper, especially in its current state of nervousness.
SECONDARY SOVEREIGN TRADE saw Brazil widen dramatically.
Brazil's 8.875 percent global bond due 2001 ZQ4P widened to the 195 bp range after beginning the week at 158 bps over.
By comparison, Mexico's 9.75 percent global due 2001 ZM5W was trading at 162 bps over, and Argentina's 9.25 percent global due 2001 ZN4D was trading at 138 over on Monday, traders said.
